title: DPO Vendor Assurance — Lite Template (contractual checklist + sample clauses)
content:
Purpose:
This lightweight template is intended for use by Data Protection Officers (DPOs) and contract owners when onboarding vendors that will process inference requests or telemetry for Redwood Inference. It is designed for vendors that are low-to-medium risk or for deals where a full DPA annex is not yet negotiated. The document combines a short prescreen checklist and a set of concise sample contract clauses that can be pasted into vendor agreements or statement-of-work attachments.

Scope and usage guidance:
- Use for SaaS vendors, partners, and managed-hosting providers that will receive non-sensitive inference metadata, aggregated telemetry, or routine operational logs.
- Not intended to replace an enterprise DPA or addendum for high-risk processors (e.g., vendors processing SI, PHI, or regulated PII at scale).
- Follow-up evidence: if a vendor fails any critical item in the checklist, escalate to Security for a fuller review or request remediations.

Quick prescreen checklist (yes/no):
- Does the vendor provide written proof of encryption at-rest and in-transit for tenant data?
- Do they support customer key management (bring-your-own-key / KMS integration) or documented justified exception?
- Is there documented access control (RBAC/least privilege) for production systems and logs?
- Are logs/telemetry retention controls configurable per-customer?
- Do they maintain a vulnerability disclosure policy and a cadence of patching critical CVEs?
- Do they permit periodic evidence review (e.g., SOC/ISO report or scoped questionnaire)?
- Are subprocessors disclosed and limited to a reasonably-scoped list?
- Do they commit to notification timelines for security incidents affecting our data (max 72 hours initial notice)?
- Is there an ability to export customer data in machine-readable format on reasonable notice?

If any item is unchecked, document remediation steps and request written confirmation prior to production onboarding.

Minimal evidence set to request (if checklist passes):
- Recent third-party attestation (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001) or completed vendor security questionnaire response.
- Network diagram (high level) showing separation between customer data plane and vendor management plane.
- Example audit log extract (sanitized) showing retention, redaction, and access audit entries.
- Summary of encryption key lifecycle practices or KMS integration details.

Sample contract language (concise, paste-ready)
1. Data processing and purpose limitation
“Vendor shall process Customer inference requests, telemetry, and associated logs only as necessary to provide the Services and for no other purpose. Any use of Customer data for model training, product improvement, or benchmarking requires prior written consent from Customer.”

2. Ephemeral telemetry and retention
“Vendor will retain inference telemetry and related logs only for the period necessary to provide the Services and not longer than thirty (30) days by default, unless Customer elects a longer retention schedule in writing. Vendor shall implement and document an automated deletion process for expired records and provide Customer with the deletion provenance upon request.”

3. Encryption and key management
“Vendor shall encrypt Customer data in transit and at rest using industry-standard controls. For at-rest encryption, Vendor shall provide the option for Customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK) integrated with supported KMS providers. If BYOK is not available, Vendor shall document the rationale and compensating controls.”

4. Access controls and least privilege
“Vendor shall enforce role-based access controls (RBAC) and multifactor authentication for administrative access to environments that process Customer data. Access to Customer-specific data shall be limited to persons with a documented business need and logged with immutable audit records.”

5. Subprocessor transparency
“Vendor will maintain an accessible list of subprocessors performing services that may access Customer data and will provide prior written notice of any material changes. Customer shall have the right to object to proposed subprocessors for legitimate regulatory or security reasons; failure to reach agreement permits Customer to terminate affected Services without penalty.”

6. Incident notification and cooperation
“In case of a security incident that reasonably affects Customer data confidentiality, integrity, or availability, Vendor shall provide Customer initial notice within seventy-two (72) hours of detection, with a summary of scope and planned mitigations. Vendor shall provide regular updates and cooperate with Customer’s incident response, including preservation of relevant forensic artifacts.”

7. Audit rights and evidence delivery
“Vendor shall deliver evidence of compliance at least annually: either a current SOC2 Type II/ISO27001 certificate or a completed security questionnaire. Upon reasonable notice, Vendor shall permit remote evidence review and provide redacted extracts from logs and architecture diagrams needed to verify compliance.”

8. Data portability and termination
“Upon termination or written request, Vendor shall make Customer data available for export in machine-readable form within ten (10) business days and delete residual copies within thirty (30) days unless retention is required by applicable law. Vendor shall certify destruction upon completion.”

9. Liability carveouts for derived outputs
“For avoidance of doubt, Vendor is not assumed to own or use Customer-generated outputs or derivative model artifacts beyond Service delivery, except as expressly agreed. Any use of outputs for model improvements shall require explicit written authorization and, where applicable, compensation terms.”

10. Minimal security SLA and remedy
“Vendor shall maintain reasonable security controls and make best efforts to meet Service availability commitments described in the SOW. Material security failures resulting from Vendor negligence shall be subject to remediation plans and potentially service credits; the parties shall negotiate equitable remedies in line with the relative harm.”

Implementation notes for contract owners:
- Keep this template intentionally concise — the goal is to secure basic compensating controls quickly for low-risk vendors.
- For vendors with access to any sensitive PII/PHI, escalate to Security & Legal for a full DPA and supplementary exhibits.
- When requesting evidence, prefer attestation + sample extracts over full system access; redact non-essential details but preserve sufficient context for verification.
- If Vendor resists BYOK but claims compensating controls, require a short write-up of those controls and an independent review or pen-test summary if available.

Red-lines and negotiation guidance (talking points for deals team):
- If Vendor asks to remove incident notification timing, push for 72 hours initial notice and 7-day follow-up commitment.
- If Vendor resists deletion timelines, negotiate a longer retention only with technical justification and a documented deletion/proof process.
- If Vendor proposes broad rights to use aggregated telemetry for model training, license back to Customer any derivative models that are materially trained on Customer inputs (or require opt-in).

Fallback and escalation:
- Any unresolved checklist failures or redlines that expand vendor rights over Customer data should be escalated to Security & Legal.
- For high-impact integrations (payment systems, regulated data flows, or public sector customers), do not use this lightweight template — require full DPA and in-scope audit.

Appendix: quick paste-ready clause for procurement teams
“Vendor warrants that it will not use Customer requests, prompts, or outputs to further train or improve any models, or for any commercial purpose, without Customer’s affirmative written consent. Vendor will provide reasonable evidence upon request that Customer data was excluded from any model training datasets during the contract term.”

Revision history:
- v0.1 (2024-11-06) initial draft by Sofia Martinez
- v0.2 (2024-12-10) added BYOK and retention guidance (Arjun Patel)
- v0.3 (2025-02-21) updated incident timing and portability language (Maya Chen)

Notes to reviewer:
This is intentionally narrow and designed to be used as a band-aid for low-risk vendor onboarding to avoid blocking engineering projects. Please flag any overly permissive language or missing regulatory points for EU/UK data residency or industry-specific requirements.
